messages:
maria_support: heads-up — customer AcmeAI says their app started getting 403s on embeddings after they upgraded seats a few minutes ago. UI shows ‘Invalid API key’ but the key works on other endpoints. paste of curl response below.

maria_support: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-****' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":{"code":"forbidden","message":"Access denied: billing_tier_insufficient","details":{"entitlement_check":"failed","feature":"embeddings"}}}
```

meena_eng: thanks — did they upgrade via the console or SSO seat migration? can you share org id and the API key id (masked) + approximate timestamp? this looks like a plan/entitlement gate, not an auth token problem.

maria_support: upgraded via console, org_id=org_0xACME, api_key_id=key_live_****, reported at 2025-11-03T17:02:11Z. they repro'd from Postman and got the same 403. customer insists key is valid because text-generation endpoints still work.

meena_eng: that pattern is classic: per-feature entitlement check runs at service edge and can 403 if billing cache hasn't synced seats/features for the org. gen endpoints use a different feature flag path. can you run a quick diagnostic on the entitlement service for org_0xACME? eg: 

```
# admin diag (run from infra tooling host)
curl -s -H "X-Debug-Token: redact" \
  https://entitlements.internal.redwood/v1/orgs/org_0xACME/status
# expected: {"plan":"pro","features":["generation","embeddings"],"cache_state":"synced"}
```

meena_eng: also check billing service for the plan update timestamp: `GET /admin/orgs/org_0xACME` and compare to entitlement last_synced.

sam_billing: saw a partial sync for org_0xACME at 2025-11-03T17:00:45Z. billing shows plan=pro but the entitlement-worker backoff retried and left the cache stale (last_synced=2025-11-03T16:50:05Z). error in logs: `license-sync: transient 504 to billing-catalog` so edge returned 403 because entitlement said embeddings not enabled.

maria_support: ok — customer wants immediate fix. can we force sync without doing a full cluster restart?

meena_eng: yes — do a targeted sync for the org. steps: 
1) trigger the entitlement worker to sync this org: `POST /internal/entitlements/sync?org=org_0xACME`
2) clear local edge cache for the org (edge hosts each have a prefix cache): `redis-cli -h cache-edge-1 keys "ent:org:org_0xACME:*" | xargs redis-cli -h cache-edge-1 del`
3) verify by calling the status endpoint above and then repro the embedding call.

meena_eng: sample command (run from ops runbook shell):
```
# trigger sync
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \
  https://internal.redwood/api/entitlements/sync?org=org_0xACME
# flush edge keys (be careful to target edge-1 only)
redis-cli -h cache-edge-1 --scan --pattern "ent:org:org_0xACME:*" | xargs -r redis-cli -h cache-edge-1 del
```

sam_billing: initiated targeted sync at 2025-11-03T17:04:10Z and returned 200. entitlement worker log shows `sync completed for org_0xACME, features: [generation,embeddings]` and cache updated.

ops_bot: :white_check_mark: Ticket #ZD-1429 created in zendesk for AcmeAI; runbook linked: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/entitlement-sync (internal).

maria_support: retried embedding call at 2025-11-03T17:04:45Z — customer confirms endpoint returns 200 and embeddings come back. they say UI no longer shows 'Invalid API key'. closing on customer side. :tada:

meena_eng: root cause summary for ticket: billing update succeeded but entitlement-worker experienced transient error -> stale entitlement cache on edge -> 403 for embeddings specifically. resolution: targeted sync + cache flush. recommend adding a small retry + background resync on 5xx from billing-catalog to avoid future stall.

maria_support: adding note to ticket and flagging for postmortem if we see >1 more hit in the next 24h.
